title: Syllogism
intro: Syllogism gives you statements ('All A are B', 'Some B are C') and asks which conclusions necessarily follow. The single rule that makes this reliable: draw the smallest Venn diagram that satisfies all statements, then accept a conclusion only if it holds in EVERY possible diagram. If even one valid arrangement breaks the conclusion, it does not follow. Train yourself to look for the counter-case, not the confirming one.

items.name: All A are B
items.formula: A circle sits fully inside B

items.name: No A is B
items.formula: A and B circles are separate

items.name: Some A are not B
items.formula: part of A lies outside B

items.name: Golden rule
items.formula: true only if it holds in EVERY valid diagram

topics.name: Basic Syllogism (All / Some / No)
topics.details: Start with the universal statements (All/No) — they fix the diagram. 'All A are B' puts A inside B; 'No A is B' keeps them apart. Then place the 'Some' overlaps. A conclusion follows only if it is forced in every arrangement.

solved.problem: All cats are animals. All animals are living. Conclusion: All cats are living?
solved.solution: Cats ⊂ animals ⊂ living, so cats ⊂ living. Follows.

solved.problem: All pens are blue. No blue is red. Conclusion: No pen is red?
solved.solution: Pens ⊂ blue, and blue is separate from red, so pens are separate from red. Follows.

solved.problem: Some boys are tall. All tall are strong. Conclusion: Some boys are strong?
solved.solution: The tall boys are strong, so some boys are strong. Follows.

solved.problem: All roses are flowers. Conclusion: Some flowers are roses?
solved.solution: Conversion of "All": if all roses are flowers, those roses are flowers that are roses — so some flowers are roses. Follows.

unsolved.problem: All dogs are mammals. All mammals are animals. All dogs are animals?
No fish is bird. All sparrows are birds. No sparrow is fish?
Some pens are red. All red are bright. Some pens are bright?
All A are B. Some B are A?
Some A are B. Conclusion: All A are B?

topics.name: Venn Method for Syllogism
topics.details: The diagram method removes all guesswork. Draw circles to satisfy the statements in the most general way, then test the conclusion: if you can draw even one legal diagram where it fails, reject it.

solved.problem: Some A are B. Some B are C. Conclusion: Some A are C?
solved.solution: You can draw A–B overlap and B–C overlap with A and C disjoint. So it does NOT follow.

solved.problem: All A are B. Some B are C. Conclusion: Some A are C?
solved.solution: C may overlap only the part of B outside A. Does NOT follow.

solved.problem: No A is B. Some B are C. Conclusion: Some C are not A?
solved.solution: Those B that are C are not A, so some C are not A. Follows.

solved.problem: All A are B. No B is C. Conclusion: No A is C?
solved.solution: A is inside B, B is apart from C, so A is apart from C. Follows.

unsolved.problem: Some A are B. All B are C. Some A are C?
Some A are B. Some B are C. Some A are C?
hints: Try to separate A and C.

unsolved.problem: All A are B. No C is B. No A is C?
hints: A inside B, C apart from B.

unsolved.problem: No A is B. No B is C. No A is C?
hints: A and C could still overlap.

unsolved.problem: All A are B. All A are C. Some B are C?
hints: A is common to B and C.

topics.name: Possibility Cases
topics.details: Some conclusions are phrased as possibilities ('Some A can be C', 'All B being C is a possibility'). A possibility follows if you can draw at least ONE legal diagram in which it is true — the opposite test from definite conclusions.

solved.problem: Some A are B. Possibility: All A are B?
solved.solution: Draw A fully inside B — consistent with "some". So the possibility holds.

solved.problem: All A are B. Possibility: Some B are not A?
solved.solution: B can be larger than A, leaving some B outside A. Possibility holds.

solved.problem: No A is B. Possibility: Some A are B?
solved.solution: "No A is B" forbids any overlap — the possibility cannot hold.

solved.problem: Some A are B. Possibility: No A is B?
solved.solution: "Some A are B" guarantees an overlap, so "no A is B" is impossible.

unsolved.problem: Some A are B. Possibility: All B are A?
All A are B. Possibility: All B are A?
No A is B. Possibility: All A are B?
All A are B. Possibility: Some A are not B?
Some A are not B. Possibility: All A are B?

topics.name: Either–Or Cases
topics.details: When two conclusions individually do not follow but together cover all cases (same subject–predicate, one positive and one negative), the answer is 'either I or II follows'.

solved.problem: Conclusions: I. Some A are B. II. No A is B. Neither alone follows. What is the answer?
solved.solution: They are complementary and exhaust all cases → Either I or II follows.

solved.problem: I. All A are B. II. Some A are not B. (complementary pair) — answer?
solved.solution: One must hold in any diagram → Either I or II.
Because the pair covers every possibility, so at least one is always true even though neither is individually certain.

solved.problem: I. Some A are C. II. Some A are not C. Answer if neither alone follows?
solved.solution: Complementary and exhaustive → Either I or II.

unsolved.problem: I. Some X are Y. II. No X is Y. Neither alone follows — answer?
Are "All A are B" and "Some A are not B" complementary?
Either-or needs the conclusions to share what?
If both conclusions follow definitely, is it "either-or"?
I. Some A are B. II. Some A are not B. Answer if neither alone follows?

shortcuts: Place universal (All/No) statements first; they fix the diagram.
A definite conclusion must hold in EVERY diagram — hunt for a counter-case.
A possibility needs only ONE diagram where it is true.
"All A are B" always allows "Some B are A" (conversion).
Complementary pair that neither follows alone ⇒ "Either I or II".
mistakes: Drawing only the diagram that confirms the conclusion.
Treating "Some A are B" as forcing "All A are B".
Concluding "Some A are C" from two separate "Some" overlaps.
Missing an either-or when neither conclusion follows alone.
pyq: SSC asks 2-statement, 2-conclusion items in Tier 1 and 3-statement sets with possibility/either-or in Tier 2. The Venn counter-case method handles all of them.

flashcards.q: A definite conclusion is true when?
flashcards.a: It holds in every valid diagram
At least one diagram makes it true

flashcards.q: Two "Some" overlaps ⇒ Some A are C?

summary: Syllogism is settled by Venn diagrams. Fix universals first, then test each conclusion: definite conclusions must survive every legal diagram, possibilities need just one. Use conversion of "All", spot complementary pairs for either-or, and never trust a single confirming picture.
